title: The German rules an XRechnung invoice or credit note adds to EN 16931
source: XRechnung 3.0, the German core invoice usage specification of EN 16931 maintained by the Koordinierungsstelle fuer IT-Standards (KoSIT), as its schematron release v2.6.0 (2026-09-02) states the rules for the Cross Industry Invoice syntax: src/validation/schematron/cii/XRechnung-CII-validation.sch and common.sch, read 2026-10-08. Only the rules below are ported; the others reach a file through the KoSIT validator, a separate tool. They apply when the buyer asks for XRechnung, which a German public buyer does. The KoSIT validator itself, with the XRechnung 3.0.2 configuration, runs untouched as EINV-KOSIT; it found the PEPPOL-EN16931-R001, -R010 and -R020 rules our first XRechnung missed (2026-10-09).

rules.text: An invoice or credit note for a buyer who asks for XRechnung carries the XRechnung specification identifier, the buyer reference, the payment instructions, a seller contact with name, phone and email, and the seller's and buyer's city and post code (the BR-DE rules below).
The seller's contact group (BG-6) is there.
The seller's post code (BT-38) is given.
The seller's contact names a person or a department (BT-41).
The seller's contact has a telephone number (BT-42).
The seller's contact has an email address (BT-43).
The buyer's post code (BT-53) is given.
The buyer reference (BT-10) is given; for a German public buyer it is the Leitweg-ID.
The specification identifier (BT-24) names XRechnung 3.0; the schematron gives this as a warning.
A payment by credit transfer (payment means code 30 or 58) gives the account to pay into (BG-17).

The official KoSIT validator (v1.6.3, Apache-2.0, run untouched) with the XRechnung 3.0.2 configuration of 2026-08-31 accepts the XML: the XRechnung scenario for an XRechnung, EN16931 (CII) otherwise; skipped when the validator is not installed.
The business process (BT-23) is given; the e-invoice pack writes the Peppol billing process urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0.
The buyer's electronic address (BT-49) is given; for a public buyer its Leitweg-ID under scheme 0204 when the order names no other.
The seller's electronic address (BT-34) is given; the seller contact's email when the order names no other.
